comparison: Both evaluate the overall CLEM methodological achievement (C6, C7, C71, C72). OpenEval finds the approach well-supported by experimental results. Peer reviewers explicitly praised this as 'technically groundbreaking' and 'a technical tour de force.' Strong agreement on the validity and importance of the CLEM approach itself.

Both address the drl:APEX2-mCherry transgenic line characterization (C31-C37). OpenEval finds the construct design and validation methodologically sound with only minor limitations (C36 data not shown). Peer reviewers raised significant concerns about whether APEX-cherry cells are truly HSPCs, noting validation data with cd41:GFP was 'not shown' and emphasizing this issue was 'not addressed in the revision.' Major disagreement on adequacy of transgenic line validation.

Both evaluate HSPC proliferation and colonization claims (C10-C14). OpenEval finds converging quantitative evidence with appropriate statistical significance supporting the circulation-based colonization inference. Peer reviewers did not challenge these basic characterization claims. Strong agreement on the validity of proliferation data and temporal dynamics.

Both address anatomical localization findings. OpenEval evaluates broader methodological advances (C15-C20) including light sheet imaging and EC pocket structures as well-documented. Peer reviewers specifically evaluated spatial localization (C17-C20) and accepted these findings, though requested better figure annotations. Agreement on anatomical characterization with presentation improvements needed.

Both evaluate ZO-1 tight junction claims (C23-C24). OpenEval finds the inference about tight junction formation reasonable given ZO-1 localization data. Peer reviewers explicitly rejected this interpretation, stating 'Figure 2A does not show a particular enrichment of ZO-1 expression near mCherry+ cells' and conclusions 'should be rephrased.' Major disagreement on the validity of tight junction enrichment claims.

Both evaluate HSPC-MSC proximity measurements (C25-C27). OpenEval finds quantitative distance measurements with adequate sample size (n=28) support the claims. Peer reviewers accepted these measurements but noted technical limitations in light microscopy resolution for determining if each HSPC contacts just one MSC. General agreement with acknowledged technical caveats.

Both evaluate CLEM correlation and 3D reconstruction (C40-C43). OpenEval finds successful correlation with precise alignment and detailed cellular architecture. Peer reviewers acknowledged technical achievement but raised concerns about limited sample size and generalizability, noting 'only two examples' were presented and questioning what proportion of HSPCs show this niche configuration. Agreement on technical success but disagreement on sufficiency of evidence for general conclusions.

Both evaluate ganglion-like cell identification and HSPC contacts from SBEM (C44-C49). OpenEval finds novel findings well-documented with extensive manual tracing. Peer reviewers expressed concerns about identifying cells without independent markers, noting HSPCs were identified as 'morphologically resembling an HSPC' and that identification remains 'preliminary' without unequivocal markers. Disagreement on adequacy of morphology-based identification.

Both evaluate morphological HSPC identification in SBEM (C50-C52). OpenEval finds morphological criteria sufficient but acknowledges uncertainty about cell identity without independent molecular markers. Peer reviewers stated 'confirmation that these are HSPCs using the reporter lines seems required' and noted only few examples were shown. Agreement that morphology-based identification has limitations requiring validation.

Both evaluate Workflow #2 results and heterogeneity (C53-C58, with R10 also including C59). OpenEval finds good correlation and consistent quantitative analysis, noting heterogeneity is well-supported by data range. Peer reviewers raised concerns that heterogeneity was 'not quantitatively appreciated,' noting only 3 of 22 HSPCs contacted glial cells and that the manuscript should better acknowledge qualitative nature and limitations. Agreement on heterogeneity existence but disagreement on adequacy of quantitative characterization.

Both evaluate functional role of ganglion-like cells and dopamine signaling (C61-C66). OpenEval finds converging evidence from imaging and 6-OHDA perturbation with appropriate controls supporting functional role. Peer reviewers accepted 6-OHDA data but raised concerns that direct contact evidence is insufficient (only '1 couple of cells' shown), HSPC identity not unequivocal, and alternative explanations for effects should be considered. Partial agreement: functional perturbation accepted but direct mechanistic evidence deemed preliminary.

OpenEval evaluates functional heterogeneity inference (C59, C8, C75) as uncertain/speculative requiring validation. Peer R10 addresses broader heterogeneity concerns including C59, emphasizing inadequate quantitative appreciation. Both recognize heterogeneity claims need stronger support, though peer reviewers focus more on quantitative characterization while OpenEval emphasizes need for functional validation.

Both evaluate Runx reporter line characterization (C21). OpenEval identifies internal inconsistency in the claim suggesting an error in extraction or manuscript text, marking it unsupported. Peer reviewers noted confusion about which reporter should be used and questioned why Runx:GFP (described as better marker) was least used. Both identify problems with reporter line characterization and communication.

OpenEval evaluated technical limitation motivating APEX2 approach (C30) as supported by authors' experience and citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific technical justification claim.
OpenEval evaluated technical SBEM method (C38) as supported by citation and successful dataset acquisition. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific technical method claim.

OpenEval evaluated anatomical feature correlation between modalities (C39) as supported, noting it validates alignment approach. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific correlation validation claim.
